title: games.fun Studio v2 pitch (out/pitch.json)
description: What a pitch or refine job writes (research/studio-v2/BUILD_JOB.md §2). A pitch job gives 2–3 cards; a refine job may narrow to 1. Every card carries a complete game spec (game-spec.schema.json) that assumes each question's default answer. The worker validates this file, and Studio shows it as cards, questions and a reply.

reply.description: One or two sentences to the creator in the chat: what changed, or what the agent decided once the question budget ran out. When a core feature of a game the creator named is missing from the kit (research.signature), the reply starts with it.

id.description: Stable within the conversation, e.g. 'a', 'b', 'c'. A refine keeps an id when it revises that card.

hook.description: One line: why this is fun with friends.

players.description: e.g. '2–4 friends; bots fill empty seats'.

conceptPrompt.description: A prompt for a concept image of this card (an image model, later).

fit.description: faithful: a faithful take on the game the creator named (its signature loop mapped onto the kit; card 1 whenever the prompt names a game, checked). variation: a different take. Only when the prompt names an existing game.

questions.description: At most 3 across the whole conversation (the job's request.json says how many are left). Each applies to whichever card the creator picks.

set.description: Optional: what picking this option changes in the chosen card's spec, as JSON pointer → value (e.g. {"/round/seconds": 180}). When every picked option has `set` (or is the default) and the creator typed nothing, the worker locks the spec without an agent.

default.description: The id of the option the cards' specs already assume.

bank.description: Research bank entry ids or paths consulted (node research/bank/search.mjs).

signature.description: When the creator names existing games: their signature loop, researched from real sources (each game's store page plus one gameplay description: a wiki, a guide or a review that says how it plays), as rows the kit supports, approximates or is missing. The checker (studio-worker/tools/check-v2.mjs) holds card 1 to it: card 1 is fit 'faithful', every missing row is in its v1.notYet, and the reply leads with a missing core feature.

bank.description: The id of the research bank entry that is our own study of this game (bank.json: "study": true). With it no url is needed: the checker takes the study as the source. Without it the checker asks for two sites.

urls.description: The store page and at least one gameplay description from another site (two sites, checked), unless bank names our own study of the game.

loop.description: One sentence: what a player does minute to minute, from those sources.

feature.description: One thing that makes it that game, e.g. 'side-scrolling levels you clear screen by screen'.

how.description: supported or approximated: which catalog mechanic, world or look does it, and how close; missing: what the kit lacks.

core.description: true for the 2-4 features without which it is not that game.

ok.description: true when the cards are within policy (PLAN §7). false only with no cards worth building; then write out/failure.txt instead.

steered.description: What was changed to keep it within policy, in words the creator reads.
